(a) 
The Secretary shall, from time to time during the calendar year, determine whether, in view of the current inventories of sugar, the estimated production from the acreage of sugarcane or sugar beets planted, the normal marketings within a calendar year of new-crop sugar, and other pertinent factors, any domestic area, the Republic of the Philippines, or Cuba, will be unable to market the quota for such area. If the Secretary finds that any domestic area or Cuba will be unable to market the quota for such area for the calendar year then current, he shall revise the quotas for the domestic areas and Cuba by prorating an amount of sugar equal to the deficit so determined to the other such areas on the basis of the quotas then in effect: 
Provided, however, That domestic areas shall not share in any deficit of any domestic area if the then outstanding determination of the Secretary made pursuant to section 201 of the Act is less than seven million short tons, raw value. If the Secretary finds that the Republic of the Philippines will be unable to market the quota for such area for the calendar year then current, he shall revise the quotas for Cuba and foreign countries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Philippines by prorating an amount of sugar equal to the deficit so determined, as follows:


 
  To Cuba ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋
  95 per centum
 
 
  To foreign countries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Philippines ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋
  5 per centum
 



Provided, however, That whenever the quota for Cuba established under the provisions of this Act other than section 202 (d) is less than the amount required by the provisions of section 202 (d) of this Act, such prorations shall be as follows:


 
  To Cuba ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋
  98. 64 per centum
 
 
  To foreign countries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Phillppines ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋ ₋
  1. 36 per centum
 



 Any portion of such Philippine deficit which the Secretary determines cannot be supplied by Cuba shall be prorated to foreign countries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Philippines. No part of any Philippine deficit so prorated may be filled by direct-consumption sugar.
 
    (b) 

If, on the 1st day of September in any calendar year, any part or all of the proration to any foreign country of the quota for foreign count ries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Philippines established under the provisions of section 202 (c) has not been filled, the Secretary may revise the proration of such quota among such foreign countries by allotting an amount of sugar equal to such unfilled proration to such foreign countries as have filled their prorations or such quota by such date. 
    (c) 

The quota for any domestic area, the Republic of the Philippines, Cuba, or other foreign countries as established under the provisions of section 202 shall not be reduced by reason of any determination of a deficit existing in any calendar year under the provisions of subsections (a) and (b) of this section 204.
 
    (d) 

Any proration among foreign countries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Philippines pursuant to this section shall be on such basis as the Secretary shall determine.

fable.w: The section directs the Secretary to determine sugar quota deficits and reallocate them by fixed percentages or on a basis the Secretary alone decides. The tempting reading is that references to domestic areas, Cuba, the Philippines and other foreign countries bring outside parties into the decision, but they are only the subjects of the quota determinations and are not consulted, heard, or given a right to object. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, express rulemaking requirement, or right to sue.
fable.s: Any proration among foreign countries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Philippines pursuant to this section shall be on such basis as the Secretary shall determine.

qwen_block.w: This section describes a unilateral administrative process where the Secretary of Agriculture determines sugar quotas and prorates deficits based on market data and inventories. There is no requirement for the Secretary to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from outside parties (such as foreign governments, domestic producers, or the public) before making these determinations. The decision-making authority rests entirely within the federal executive branch.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall, from time to time during the calendar year, determine whether... any domestic area, the Republic of the Philippines, or Cuba, will be unable to market the quota for such area. If the Secretary finds that any domestic area or Cuba will be unable to market the quota for such area for the calendar year then current, he shall revise the quotas...

opus.w: The section lets the Secretary decide alone whether there are sugar quota deficits and how to reallocate them. It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. The tempting reading treats the named domestic areas and foreign countries as participants, but they only receive the reallocated quotas. They play no part in making the decision, so the federal boundary is never crossed.
opus.s: Any proration among foreign countries other than Cuba and the Republic of the Philippines pursuant to this section shall be on such basis as the Secretary shall determine.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section names outside parties, including domestic producing areas, the Republic of the Philippines, Cuba and other foreign countries, so it may seem to involve outsiders. But these parties only receive quota allocations. The statute never has the Secretary consult them, hold a hearing, take public comment, issue regulations or give them a right to object or sue. Every decision here ("such basis as the Secretary shall determine") is made by the Secretary alone.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines a unilateral administrative process where the Secretary determines quota adjustments based on market data and estimates. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any outside parties (such as foreign governments, producers, or the public) before making the decision. The involvement of foreign countries is as recipients of the regulatory decision, not as participants in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall, from time to time during the calendar year, determine whether, in view of the current inventories of sugar, the estimated production from the acreage of sugarcane or sugar beets planted, the normal marketings within a calendar year of new-crop sugar, and other pertinent factors, any domestic area, the Republic of the Philippines, or Cuba, will be unable to market the quota for such area.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary's determination involves "pertinent factors" which could implicitly include input from outside parties, or that the revision of quotas affects foreign countries (outside entities) and thus requires their participation. However, the text describes a unilateral administrative calculation by the Secretary based on market data (inventories, production estimates). There is no requirement for consultation, comment periods, hearings, or advisory boards involving non-federal actors. The foreign countries are subjects of the regulation, not participants in the decision-making process.
